title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
hints: Two pointers, one per array — both arrays are already sorted.
Repeatedly append the smaller front element and advance that pointer; append the leftovers at the end.
`while i < a.count && j < b.count { … }` then `result += a[i...]; result += b[j...]`.
jsBridge: The same algorithm as in JS. The Swift twist is that you can't index past the end silently: JS returns `undefined` and your comparison quietly goes false, while Swift traps. So bounds-checking in the loop condition is mandatory.

compass.q: `a[i] < b[j]` when `i` is out of range is `undefined < 5`, which is false in JS. What does Swift do, and which bugs does that catch early?
Two-pointer merge O(n+m) vs `(a + b).sorted()` O((n+m)log(n+m)): Swift's sort is Timsort-like and fast on nearly sorted input. Does that change your answer?
Merging two sorted feeds (local cache and server page) is a real app task. How do you handle duplicates by ID?
Can you write this generically for any `Comparable` sequence, not just arrays? What does that buy you?
